_: NAMED, DELIBERATE-OR-SUSPECTED DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THIS ENGINE AND A VENDOR. Read tests/fixtures/vendor/README.md first. A row here is what lets `tools/vendor_truth.py` say 'this delta is EXPLAINED' instead of 'this delta is a bug' — so a row that is wrong is worse than no row at all, because it launders a real defect into an expected one.

_status_vocabulary.suspected: DERIVED FROM OUR CODE, NOT YET MEASURED AGAINST THE VENDOR. We can state exactly what WE do, and we have a documented reason to believe the vendor does otherwise — but nobody has read the vendor's number. ⛔ A `suspected` row NEVER explains a delta: `vendor_truth.py` counts a delta matching one as UNEXPLAINED-BUT-ANTICIPATED and still reports it, because an unmeasured belief that silences a measurement is the exact defect this directory exists to prevent.
_status_vocabulary.confirmed: MEASURED. An observation in `observations/` exhibits this delta and its `explains` names this row. Only a `confirmed` row may explain a delta.
_status_vocabulary.refuted: MEASURED, AND WE MATCH THE VENDOR AFTER ALL. Kept rather than deleted — a retired suspicion is the cheapest thing to re-suspect, and the next reader deserves to know it was checked. Carries `refutedBy`.
_status_vocabulary.accepted: CONFIRMED, AND WE ARE KEEPING OUR BEHAVIOUR ON PURPOSE. Requires `decision` — who ruled, when, and why. This is the row type that MUST reach a member: an accepted divergence is a sentence the product owes whoever pasted the script.
_status_vocabulary.spec-falsified: MEASURED AGAINST THE VENDOR'S PUBLISHED DEFINITION and found to differ, by `tools/vendor_spec_probes.py`. Stronger than `suspected` (a number was computed, not a belief stated) and weaker than `confirmed` (nobody has read the vendor's SCREEN, and prose can be incomplete). ⛔ It still may not explain a delta in `vendor_truth.py` — the asymmetry is deliberate: a falsified spec probe says we are probably wrong, which is a reason to FIX, never a reason to expect.
_status_vocabulary.corrected: MEASURED, WE DIFFERED, AND WE CHANGED OURS TO MATCH THE VENDOR. ⛔⛔ THIS TERM EXISTS BECAUSE THE LEDGER COULD NOT SAY THE MOST COMMON GOOD OUTCOME. It could say `accepted` (we differ and are keeping ours) and `refuted` (we thought we differed and never did) — but a divergence we CLOSED by fixing our own side had nowhere to live, so `rsi-zero-movement-reads-na` was filed `accepted` and two rails correctly refused it: an accepted row owes a member a `vendorNote`, and after a correction there is no difference left to disclose. Forcing it into `accepted` would have made the ledger assert the opposite of what happened. ⭐ KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, for `refuted`'s reason turned around: the next reader needs to know the old behaviour existed, that it was deliberate, and what argument retired it — otherwise they re-introduce it. Requires `decision` (`ruled` — who and when; `what_changed` — the behaviour now) and `correctedIn` (the commit). ⛔ IT OWES A MEMBER NOTHING, and that is the whole difference from `accepted`: once ours matches the vendor there is no sentence the product owes anybody. A `vendorNote` here would describe a difference that no longer exists.

_probe_rule: ⛔ EVERY ROW CARRIES A `probe` THAT DISCRIMINATES. The probe describes a case whose VALUE DIFFERS under the two conventions, with the two answers named. A row whose probe cannot distinguish the conventions is a description of nothing — `lesson_a_fixture_that_cannot_distinguish_is_not_a_rail` — and `test_vendor_truth.py` refuses a row that does not carry both answers.

rows.ours: True Range is defined from bar 1 — `compute_atr_raw` loops `for i in range(1, n)`, so bar 0 contributes NO TR. The seed is the simple mean of the first `period` TRs (i.e. TR of bars 1..period) and lands on `bars[period]`.
rows.theirs: Pine's `ta.atr(length)` is documented as `ta.rma(ta.tr(true), length)`, and `ta.tr(true)` DEFINES bar 0 as `high - low` rather than leaving it `na`. Their TR array therefore starts one bar earlier and contains one value ours does not.
rows.why_it_matters: Two differences compose: the seed is the mean of a DIFFERENT SET of true ranges, and it lands one bar EARLIER. Wilder smoothing decays a seed difference rather than erasing it, so the delta is largest at the left edge and shrinks rightward — which means a fixture window chosen too far right will show agreement that is not there. ⚠️ ATR is an input to stops, position sizing and supertrend, so an early-bars delta propagates into a LATCHING difference wherever it feeds a state machine.

probe.case: ATR(14) on the FIRST 20 bars of a series, read at bar 14 and bar 15
probe.under_ours: bar 14 is the first non-empty value, and it is mean(TR[1..14])
probe.under_theirs: bar 13 is the first non-empty value, and it is mean(TR[0..13]) where TR[0] = high[0] - low[0]
probe.discriminates: the two conventions disagree about WHICH BAR first carries a value, which is visible without comparing any float at all — and then about the value itself

measured.alignment: our first value lands on bar 14; the published definition's on bar 13 — ONE BAR LATE, on every series, forever
measured.calibration: ⭐ THE SAME RUN AGREED ON THREE OTHER PROBES — `sma(close,20)` to 4.3e-14, `ema(close,10)` to 0, `rma(close,14)` to 9.9e-14. That is what makes this finding credible rather than an artefact: the instrument that reports ATR wrong reports the smoother it is built on RIGHT, so the disagreement is in the true-range half and not in the harness.

decay.note: the VALUE defect decays; the ALIGNMENT defect (one fewer emitted value) does not.

decision.ruled: 2026-08-29 — KEEP OURS. Wilder's original stands; we do not move it for this.
decision.prior_ruling: ⛔⛔ THIS WAS ALREADY ADJUDICATED, and the adjudication is a test: `tests/test_ast_indicators.py::test_our_atr_IS_WILDER_and_the_difference_from_pine_is_the_SEED`. It answered a cross-product finding that our ATR 'matches neither Wilder RMA nor SMA-of-TR — a third convention', proved ours IS Wilder's exactly (with the SMA-of-TR alternative computed as a DISAGREEING control), identified this same bar-0 mechanism by name, and warned in its own words: “a cross-product probe must not sample the warm-up — 0.20 vs 0.21 read at bar 15 is two seeds, not two formulas, and reading it as a formula difference is how a correct implementation gets ‘fixed’.”
decision.what_happened: ⚰️ I DID EXACTLY THAT, and it is recorded rather than quietly reverted. `probe_atr` measured the delta, I changed `compute_atr_raw` and `computeATR` to the published `ta.rma(ta.tr(true), n)` form, the probes went 4/4 green — and the golden fixtures went red by design (`atr_14`, `atr_bands_14_2`, `test_hand_computed_atr`), which is how the prior ruling surfaced. Reverted the same session.
why_keep_ours: OURS IS CORRECT WILDER. This is not a bug being tolerated; it is one valid convention beside another. TradingView's `ta.atr` is Wilder smoothing over a TR series that includes bar 0; ours is Wilder smoothing over a TR series that starts where a true range is actually defined. Neither is wrong about Wilder.

THE DELTA IS INVISIBLE WHERE IT IS READ. Measured over 300 bars: 0.233% at the seed, 0.079% by bar 30, 0.0022% by bar 80, 4.4e-12 by bar 299. A chart shows thousands of bars; nothing a member looks at differs.

THE CONSUMERS THAT WOULD MOVE ARE NOT THE PASTE SURFACE. `compute_atr_raw` feeds supertrend, `screener/technicals` (atr_pct, a50), `screener/bar_character`, `alert_series`'s armed member alerts, and the chart overlay. Those want the firm's own convention and have no stake in TradingView parity; changing them to serve the import lane would move live stops, sizing and saved-scan results for a difference of 4e-12 where it is read.

A SECOND, VENDOR-FAITHFUL `atr` IS THE WORSE ANSWER. Two entries computing 'the ATR' is a second authority over one value — this repo's most repeated defect — and the member could not tell which one their formula got.
decision.what_would_reopen_it: A member reporting a visible mismatch against a TradingView chart; OR a scan surface whose fetch window is short enough that the one missing value matters (measured: on a 16-bar fetch we emit 2 values where the published definition emits 3 — the ALIGNMENT half never decays). Either would change the arithmetic of this decision, not just the mood.
decision.owed_to_the_member: ⛔ STILL OPEN. An accepted divergence is a sentence the product owes whoever pasted the script, and no surface says it yet. Tracked as X-VENDOR-1.

rows.ours: `_smooth_col` accumulates until it has `n` finite values, then seeds `prev = total / n` — the SMA of the first full window — and emits its first value AT that bar. `ema` passes alpha = 2/(n+1), `rma` passes 1/n; both share the seed by construction.
rows.theirs: TradingView documents `ta.ema` as seeded from `ta.sma(source, length)`, which we believe MATCHES. Recorded anyway because the belief is documentation-derived and untested, and because the seeding rule is the single highest-leverage unmeasured decision in the engine: an engine seeded with the first close instead of the window SMA produces a curve that converges to ours and is wrong forever at the left edge.
rows.why_it_matters: If this is wrong, EVERY `ema`, `rma`, `rsi`, `atr`, `adx` and anything composed from them is wrong at the left edge, and all of them decay toward agreement — so the error is invisible in any fixture window that starts late. This is the divergence most likely to be missed by a careless harness.

probe.case: EMA(10) read at the bar where it FIRST becomes non-empty
probe.under_ours: the first value equals the arithmetic mean of the first 10 closes, exactly
probe.under_theirs_if_different: a first-close seed would make the first emitted value equal `close[0]` smoothed 9 times toward the later closes — a different number, and a different first bar
probe.discriminates: the first emitted value is a pure function of the seeding rule, so one float at one bar separates the conventions

rows.refutedBy: tools/vendor_spec_probes.py::probe_ema and ::probe_rma, 2026-08-29. An independent implementation of TradingView's published seeding (SMA of the first `length` values, first value on bar `length - 1`) agrees with ours to 0 and 9.9e-14 respectively, on the same 80-bar series, with matching first bars. ⭐ KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED: this was the highest-leverage unmeasured decision in the engine, and the next reader deserves to know it was checked rather than re-suspect it. ⚠ The check is against their PROSE, not their screen — a real observation could still surprise us.

rows.ours: A non-finite input RESETS the smoother — `prev, count, total = NAN, 0, 0.0` — so the series re-seeds after a hole rather than carrying state across it. The docblock argues this: an EMA that carried state across a hole would report an average over bars it never saw.
rows.theirs: MEASURED 2026-09-08, AND THEY HOLD. TradingView keeps the smoother's state UNCHANGED across an `na` source bar: the output is `na` AT that bar and the very next finite bar takes ONE normal step from the pre-hole state. Verified on all four `na` holes of a 400-bar SPY 1D capture, for BOTH ta.ema(.,10) and ta.rma(.,10): the hold prediction reproduces the vendor to 0 or 1.1e-13, and the vendor emits a value on the very next bar where our reset requires a further 9 blank bars before re-seeding.
rows.why_it_matters: It is reachable from a composed series — `ema(sma(close,20), 9)` has a 19-bar hole by construction, which is the warm-up of the inner window, so EVERY composed smoother in the product meets this rule on its left edge.

probe.case: EMA(5) over a series with one `na` planted in the middle
probe.under_ours: the output is empty for n-1 bars after the hole, then restarts from a fresh window SMA
probe.under_carry_state: the output continues on the next finite bar with no gap, from the pre-hole state
probe.discriminates: the COUNT of empty bars after the hole (9 vs 0 for n=10), which is countable rather than compared -- and then the resumed VALUE, which pins the mechanism rather than just the gap
probe.under_theirs: MEASURED: the output is empty for exactly ONE bar (the hole itself) and resumes immediately at the pre-hole state stepped once by the new value

rows._we_are_wrong: ⛔⛔ THIS IS A SHIPPED-CHART DEFECT, NOT A DESIGN CHOICE. Our smoothers reset on `na`; TradingView holds. It is DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN 2F-2C: changing `smoothCol` changes the columnar lane's output on every chart whose source carries a mid-series hole, which is an owner ruling and not a runtime wave's to make unilaterally. The runtime therefore MATCHES THE COLUMNAR LANE (one authority, one divergence, recorded once) rather than matching the vendor while the chart does not. ⚠️ Blast radius is narrower than it looks: before the first finite value there is no state to hold, so a LEFT-EDGE hole (the warm-up of a composed inner window, e.g. `ema(sma(close,20),9)`) answers the same either way. The two rules differ only for a hole AFTER state exists.
rows.decision_required: Owner ruling: fix `smoothCol` to hold (vendor-faithful, changes shipped chart output at mid-series holes) or record as `accepted`.

rows.ours: `x - y * trunc(x / y)` in both lanes — truncated division, so the result carries the sign of the DIVIDEND: `mod(-7, 3)` is -1, not 2.
rows.theirs: TradingView's own operator page warns that `%` on negatives may differ from other languages, which is a warning rather than a specification. Low confidence in both directions until measured.
rows.why_it_matters: Narrow: it is only reachable on a negative dividend, and most indicator arithmetic is on prices. Recorded because it is cheap to check once a chart is open, and because a `%` divergence is the kind that produces an occasional wrong bar rather than a wrong curve — the hardest kind to notice.

probe.case: `mod(close - open, 3)` on a bar where `close < open`
probe.discriminates: the SIGN differs, which is visible at a glance and cannot be a rounding artefact

rows.ours: `hma(src, n)` uses `floor(n / 2)` for the half-window and `round(sqrt(n))` for the smoothing window, each clamped at 1.
rows.theirs: TradingView's `ta.hma` restates Alan Hull's published definition, which is the same `floor(n / 2)`. WE MATCH — this row is `confirmed` as AGREEMENT, and it is here because the agreement was nearly broken by our own refusal advice.
rows.why_it_matters: ⚰️ `pine.js::fractionalWindowAdvice` told members to write `round(n * 1/2)`, which is 28 where `hma(close, 55)` uses 27 — measured 0.636 apart over 140 bars. A member following our own advice built a different indicator under the same name. Fixed 2026-08-29 (`ba78a1e27`), railed by `pine.windowAdvice.test.js`, which MEASURES the two expansions against `hma` rather than reading the sentence.

probe.under_round: differs from `wma(2*wma(close,28) - wma(close,55), 7)` by up to 0.636 on the same series
probe.discriminates: measured in `pine.windowAdvice.test.js`, with the second assertion as the control that makes the first mean something

rows.ours: `interpret(ast, bars)` computes a Wilder/RMA-recursive function (e.g. `rsi`, `atr`) using ONLY the bars it is handed. Its first computable value (bar `period`) is seeded from a SIMPLE mean of just the first `period` diffs/true-ranges inside that window -- it has no knowledge of any bar before the window's own start.
rows.theirs: TradingView's `ta.rsi`/`ta.atr` run continuously over a symbol's REAL, often decades-long chart history. The real vendor value at any given calendar bar already reflects that entire prior smoothing history, not a fresh seed at whatever date a capture happens to start.
rows.why_it_matters: ⚠️ THIS IS A CAPTURE-METHODOLOGY ARTIFACT, NOT A FORMULA DISAGREEMENT, and it is exactly the misclassification risk `VENDOR_PARITY_TRANCHE_2_READINESS_REPORT.md` named before any capture was made: comparing UCT's freshly-cold-seeded early bars against a vendor's already-converged value at the SAME calendar date can show a LARGE relative delta (measured up to ~25% at bar 14 of a 1,328-bar real SPY capture) that has nothing to do with the two engines disagreeing about the formula -- both use Wilder recursion identically, and the delta decays as UCT's own recursion catches up. This is a DIFFERENT, larger effect than (and confounds any attempt to isolate) the small, already-adjudicated `atr-tr-starts-at-bar-1` bar-0/TR-definition difference (~0.23% at ITS seed) -- the two must not be conflated. Applies to ANY Wilder/RMA-seeded function captured over a finite real-market window, not just rsi/atr specifically.

probe.case: rsi(close,14) at bar index 14 of a 1,328-bar real SPY Daily capture (2021-05-24..2026-09-04) vs. the real vendor's ta.rsi(close,14) value at that same calendar bar
probe.under_ours: 68.78150014823609 -- seeded fresh from only the 14 diffs inside this capture window
probe.under_theirs: 68.16309777289919 -- the real vendor's value, reflecting continuous smoothing since well before this window began
probe.discriminates: a ~0.9% delta at bar 14 that shrinks to ~1e-9 (float noise) by bar 180 of the SAME series as UCT's own recursion converges -- a decay curve, not a persistent formula disagreement, and reproduced with near-identical shape/magnitude on atr(high,low,close,14) over the same bars

measured.note: both converge to <1e-6 relative delta permanently by bar 180; see VENDOR_PARITY_TRANCHE_2_LANE_A_RSI_ATR_REPORT.md for the full per-checkpoint decay table

rows.ours: Before 2F-2C the runtime could not execute a recurrent builtin at all, so there was no behaviour to agree or disagree with. 2F-2C implements the measured rule directly: carried state advances INSIDE the call, so a skipped call site does not step it.
rows.theirs: MEASURED 2026-09-08. A recurrent builtin inside a UDF called on only some chart bars steps ONLY on the bars where the call executes. Stepping every chart bar with the held input is EXCLUDED: it would make the conditional result equal an every-bar EMA of the same source, and the vendor's two series differ on every executed bar.
rows.why_it_matters: It is the opposite indexing from P7.2's ruling for function-local SERIES HISTORY, which is chart-bar indexed and HOLDS across skipped bars. History holds; recurrence does not advance. Building recurrence on the end-of-bar commit phase -- the obvious reuse of the history machinery -- would silently implement the excluded model.
rows.code: runtime/vm.js::OP.CARRIED (steps inside the call, never from the commit phase)

probe.case: `f(v) => ta.ema(v, 5)` called only on even bars, beside `ta.ema(close, 5)` called every bar
probe.under_ours: the conditional series is an EMA of the even-bar subsequence
probe.under_theirs_if_different: an every-bar model would make the two series equal on executed bars
probe.discriminates: six consecutive executed invocations reproduce to err=0.000e+00 under invocation-stepping, and the two series differ on every one of them

rows.refutedBy: Implemented to match the measured vendor rule in 2F-2C; kept as the record of which model was excluded and by what evidence.

rows.ours: `rolling` emits NaN for a window containing ANY NaN, and `interpret.js`'s header states the rule out loud: "any NaN INSIDE a window makes that window's output NaN". So over a gappy source our `sma`/`wma`/`stdev`/`highest`/... go blank on the hole AND for the `n-1` bars that still contain it.
rows.theirs: MEASURED 2026-09-08. `ta.sma(gappy, 10)` answers on EVERY bar, including the `na` bars, and its value is the mean of the last 10 FINITE values of the source - reaching back over as many BARS as that requires. 370 matches, 0 mismatches, worst delta 0.0 over a 400-bar SPY 1D capture with 133 na bars. An `na` is SKIPPED, never propagated and never treated as zero. ⛔ AND THE FAMILY DOES NOT SHARE ONE RULE — measured 2026-09-08 across all twelve members: sma/stdev/sum/median SKIP (last n FINITE observations, answering on the na bar); dev PROPAGATES (clean n-BAR window); highest/lowest RESTART (the window begins again after a hole). wma fits none of five hypotheses and is UNRESOLVED; highestbars/lowestbars answer ON the na bar, a fourth shape; rising/falling were not determined by the probe.
rows.why_it_matters: It is the SAME class of defect as `nan-restarts-the-smoother` but wider: it reaches all twelve `FINITE_WINDOW` members in BOTH lanes, and it is reachable from any conditional source (`cond ? x : na`), any `valuewhen`, any pivot - all ordinary Pine. ⛔ AND THE TWO FAMILIES DIFFER FROM EACH OTHER: a window SKIPS an na and still answers; a recurrence WITHHOLDS its answer for that bar but keeps its state. One rule cannot be applied to both.

probe.under_ours: blank on the na bar and on the following 9 bars - the source's 267 finite bars yield far fewer outputs
probe.under_theirs: a value on all 400 bars, equal to the mean of the last 10 finite source values
probe.discriminates: the COUNT of answered bars (133 vs 0 on na bars) before any value is compared, and then the value itself

rows._owner_ruling_required: ✅ RULED 2026-09-08: fix it. Corrected for the six members whose rule is proven, in BOTH lanes and in the runtime. The row stays `confirmed` rather than `refuted` because FOUR members are still on the pre-existing policy with their true rule unknown — see gap register PART Z, Z7.2 and Z7.3. A family is not vendor-complete while a third of it is unmeasured.

rows.shape: A hole in the source destroys the shipped composites, in three different ways.
rows.ours: `computeRSI` booked a non-finite diff as gain 0 / loss 0, which decays BOTH Wilder averages and leaves their RATIO unchanged -- so the printed value repeated the previous bar and read exactly like a hold while the state underneath had been scaled down. Every later bar was then wrong and never re-converged (bar 42 read 74.94 against a true 78.97; bar 79 was still off). `computeATR`, `computeMACD` and `computeADX` instead went NaN and STAYED NaN -- NaN is absorbing through their recursions -- so one hole blanked the series from that bar to the end of the chart. And in all four, an `na` inside the SEED window made the seed itself NaN and the output was empty: `finite = 0` over 300 bars. `computeADX` additionally FABRICATED directional movement, booking a confident zero for a bar whose +DM/-DM could not be computed.
rows.theirs: TradingView HOLDS. `ta.rsi` is an `rma` of gains and losses and `ta.macd` an `ema` difference, so both inherit the smoother rule pinned on 2026-09-08: `na` at the hole, state unchanged, one normal step on the next finite bar. `ta.rsi` loses TWO bars because `ta.change` reads the hole as its previous value; `ta.macd` loses one. 380 of 380 bars on the na SHAPE, and the values reconstruct to 1.3e-6 with the residual decaying ~2 orders per 60 bars (seed truncation, not a model gap).
rows.why_it_matters: These are the four most-used indicators in the product and the RSI form is the dangerous one: it left NO GAP on the chart. A member saw a continuous, plausible line that had been wrong since the last hole, with nothing to indicate it.

probe.case: UCTPROBE_COMPOSITE_A: `ta.rsi(gc,14)`, `ta.macd(gc,12,26,9)` and `ta.ema(gc,14)` over `gc = bar_index % 11 == 0 ? na : close`, SPY 1D
probe.under_ours: `rsi` answers on EVERY bar including the holes, with a value that repeats the previous bar and is wrong from there on; `macd` is blank from the first hole to the end of the chart. Over 80 bars with holes every 11, `macd`/`atr`/`adx` returned finite=0 -- nothing at all -- because a hole also landed inside the seed.
probe.under_theirs: `rsi` is blank on the hole AND on the bar after it, then resumes from the pre-hole state; `macd` is blank on the hole only and resumes on the very next bar. 380 of 380 bars.
probe.discriminates: the na SHAPE alone, before any value is compared: our `rsi` never blanks and their `rsi` blanks twice per hole, and our `macd` never recovers while theirs recovers in one bar. The values then confirm it -- reconstructing from the HOLD rule matches to 1.3e-6 with the residual decaying ~2 orders per 60 bars.

rows.shape: `ta.rising`/`ta.falling` were implemented as finite windows and belong to the carried family.
rows.ours: A strict-monotone scan over `length + 1` samples with a uniform NaN-anywhere-in-the-window rule -- the residual gap the 2026-09-06 resolution disclosed for both members.
rows.theirs: A COUNTER of consecutive strict steps that HOLDS across an `na`, reported as `count >= length`. 375ok/0bad on three independent sources; RESET-on-na scores 287/88; every window policy fails (skip 323/52, forward-fill 291/84, propagate 287/88).
rows.why_it_matters: No na policy could ever have fixed this. Two bars of the capture present STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL windows -- an `na` followed by four strictly rising values -- and TradingView answers TRUE at one and FALSE at the other. The visible signature: the source DROPS from 7 to 1 across a hole and `ta.rising` stays true, because the hole held the count.

probe.case: UCTPROBE_RISEFALL_C: `ta.rising(vm, 4)` over `vm = bar_index % 11 == 0 ? na : bar_index % 8`, SPY 1D
probe.under_ours: a strict-monotone scan of the last 5 samples with NaN-anywhere-blanks: false wherever the window touches a hole, and after the sawtooth wraps.
probe.under_theirs: true across the hole even when the source DROPS through it -- 7 at one bar, `na`, then 1, and `rising` is still true -- because the counter was held rather than reset or re-evaluated.
probe.discriminates: two bars presenting STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL windows (an `na` followed by four strictly rising values) that the vendor answers TRUE and FALSE. No window-local model of any na policy can produce both, so the discriminator is the contradiction itself rather than a count.

rows.shape: `ta.highestbars`/`ta.lowestbars` returned the most recent tied extreme; the vendor returns the oldest.
rows.ours: `windowArgExtreme` walked BACKWARD from the newest bar and returned the first match -- the smallest distance back. It also used PROPAGATE for `na` and therefore blanked on a hole.
rows.theirs: Ties resolve to the OLDEST occurrence (380ok/0bad against 193ok/187bad for newest, 244 of the agreeing bars carrying no `na` at all). The `na` policy is RESTART, and the answer on an `na` bar is 0 rather than blank -- a restarted window has this bar as its only candidate, so the OFFSET is defined where the VALUE is not.
rows.why_it_matters: ⚠️ RE-MEASURED 2026-09-09 ON REAL SPY OHLCV (2,031 daily bars, the `ema-close20-2026-09-06` observation): the tie-break moves **0.4%** of `high` windows at n=5 and **0.6%** at n=14/20/25, and **0.3%** of `low` windows at every length. `aroon` moves with them — 0.6% of bars at both 14 and 25, median 7.1 points on a 0-100 scale, max 14.3. ⚰️⚰️ THIS SAID "6-10% of bars" AND IT WAS WRONG BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, at the very lengths it named. Repeated highs in a real price series are rarer than that paragraph assumed. ⛔ THE RARITY IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE RULE, NOT AGAINST IT: it is exactly why two lanes agreed on the wrong convention for so long and why the committed corpus could not see it — a defect that shows on 1 bar in 200 is one nobody finds by looking. `aroon` is built on these two and moves with them.

rows.shape: RSI of a source that never moves: this engine answered `na`, TradingView answers 100. OURS NOW ANSWERS 100 TOO.
rows.ours: ⚰️ WAS: `avg_loss == 0 AND avg_gain == 0` refused as not-computable, in BOTH lanes, pinned by a fixture and guarded by an AST single-authority rail. NOW: Pine's order — zero-LOSS tested first — so 0/0 reads 100.0 in both lanes, byte-identical to the vendor. The frozen-ticker exposure the `na` was introduced for is mitigated at the SCREENER instead: `screener/technicals.py::_rsi` reports NOT COMPUTABLE for a window whose closes never moved, which is narrower than 'flat' on purpose — `chg_pct_1d` still reports 0.00, because a change of zero is TRUE while an RSI of a motionless series is not.
rows.theirs: Pine evaluates `down == 0 ? 100 : up == 0 ? 0 : ...` -- the zero-LOSS test fires FIRST, so 0/0 reads 100. Measured directly with `ta.rsi(k, 14)` over a constant source: 100 on every bar of the capture.
rows.why_it_matters: ⚠⚠ THIS ONE REVERSES A DELIBERATE PRIOR DECISION AND RE-OPENS A NAMED INCIDENT. The `na` was introduced because on 2026-08-09 SIM, TMTS, CWEN-A, DRDB and OBA carried rsi14 = 100.0 with chg_pct_1d = 0.00, so an "RSI > 70" screen surfaced five frozen tickers as the most overbought names in the universe. The old docstring justified the refusal with "Pine's ta.rsi yields NaN here" -- a claim about the vendor that was never checked and is FALSE. The correction has been applied (Pine wins over an internal invention), but the exposure is real: the mitigation belongs at the SCREENER, which should not admit a zero-movement / zero-ADR ticker to a momentum screen, rather than in the definition of RSI. Owner ruling requested on where that guard goes.

probe.under_ours: `na` / None -- "not computable", because 0/0 is not a number.
probe.under_theirs: 100.0 on every bar of the capture.

The companion plots pin the other two corners: a monotonically rising source also reads 100 and a falling one reads 0, both of which we already matched.

rows._ruling: RESOLVED by owner ruling 2026-09-08: MATCH TRADINGVIEW. `ta.rsi` of a zero-movement source returns 100 in both lanes (`indicators.js::computeRSI`, `indicator_compute.rsi_from_wilder_averages`), because Pine tests `down == 0` FIRST and we measured 100 directly. The frozen-ticker exposure the old `na` was protecting against is handled where it belongs -- at the SCREENER: `api/services/screener/technicals.py::_rsi` now reports NOT COMPUTABLE for a series that did not move at all across the lookback, so a dead ticker cannot top an 'RSI > 70' scan. ⭐ THE GUARD IS DELIBERATELY NARROWER THAN 'FLAT': `chg_pct_1d` of a frozen ticker stays 0.00, because a change of zero is a TRUE statement about price while an RSI of a flat series is an undefined one. ⚠️ The old rule was defended in-code by the claim *"Pine's ta.rsi yields NaN here"* -- a statement about the vendor that was never checked and is false. That is the failure mode this roster exists to catch.

decision.ruled: Owner, 2026-09-08 — 'RSI ruling: approved. Match TradingView. Move the guard to the screener.'
decision.what_changed: `indicator_compute.rsi_from_wilder_averages` and `indicators.js::computeRSI` both answer 100.0 when `avg_loss == 0` (whatever `avg_gain` is) and 0.0 when `avg_gain == 0` — Pine's branch ORDER, not merely its values. The zero-movement refusal moved to `screener/technicals.py::_rsi`.
decision.why_the_old_rule_went: It was defended in-code by *'Pine's ta.rsi yields NaN here'* — a claim about the vendor that was never checked and is false. A tested invariant can still be a UCT invention: this one was pinned by a fixture, guarded by an AST rail, mirrored across both lanes, and wrong.
decision.what_would_reopen_it: A TradingView capture in which `ta.rsi` over a constant source answers anything other than 100 — or evidence that a consumer other than the screener reads this value as an overbought LEVEL and has no guard of its own. ⭐ THE SECOND CONDITION WAS RAISED, MEASURED AND RULED ON 2026-09-09; see `downstream_consumers` below. It is closed, not outstanding.

rows.correctedIn: 7e0111d94 (2026-09-08) — 2F-2D: the recurrent composites were wrong on every gap

downstream_consumers._: ⭐⭐ WHAT THE CORRECTION TOUCHED BESIDE THE SCREENER, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN AS A ROW OF ITS OWN. This is NOT a vendor divergence — after the correction our answer IS TradingView's — and this file's own opening line scopes it to *differences between this engine and a VENDOR*, warning that a wrong row *'launders a real defect into an expected one'*. A separate `accepted` row would also have demanded a `vendorNote` on `rsi`: a sentence telling members about a difference that no longer exists. So the finding lives on the row it is a CONSEQUENCE of.
downstream_consumers.what_changed_for_them: Each keeps a PRIVATE copy of the RSI calculation that calls the shared `rsi_from_wilder_averages`, so both inherited the ruling without being named in it. A window in which price never moved now reaches them as 100 where it previously reached them as `None` — and `None` is what their own guards refuse on, so the old value was rejected outright and 100 is not.

measured_2026_09_09.bullish: Gate is `current_rsi >= 35 -> return` (oversold zone). 100 fails it, so the detector CANNOT fire on a zero-movement window. No exposure.
measured_2026_09_09.bearish: Gate is `current_rsi <= 65 -> return` (overbought zone), which 100 clears. But 100 is the TOP of the scale and a bearish divergence requires the LATER peak to be weaker than the earlier one — nothing is weaker than the maximum. A halt-then-higher-high series was built to force it (rising leg, an 18-bar perfectly flat window reading RSI 100, a pullback, then a higher high at RSI 90): ZERO detections.
measured_2026_09_09.residual_not_ruled_out: ⚠️ NAMED BECAUSE IT IS UNPROVEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A halt on the EARLIER peak reads 100, which would exaggerate how far RSI fell between the two peaks and could inflate the confidence SCORE of an otherwise genuine signal. No case was constructed that demonstrates it; none was constructed that rules it out either.

downstream_consumers.ruling: Owner, 2026-09-09 — option (a): leave it, record the finding. The measured exposure is a possible score nudge on a real signal, not a fabricated signal, and the two alternatives both meant editing an OWNER-PAUSED workstream to fix something unproven.
downstream_consumers.backlog_when_that_workstream_unpauses: Remove the private RSI copies; point both divergence detectors at the shared guarded helper. The duplicated implementation is the underlying smell — the ruling reached them by inheritance precisely because nobody had to name them.

rows.ours: `barstate.ishistory` is exactly `barstate.isconfirmed`: 1 on every bar whose period has ended. This engine evaluates a STATIC FETCH — one request, one response — so every closed bar arrived the same way and there is nothing in our world that distinguishes them. `barstate.isrealtime` is 1 only on the newest bar and only while its scheduled close is still ahead of the evaluating instant, and that instant is HANDED IN rather than read off the wall clock.
rows.theirs: TradingView distinguishes a bar the chart LOADED as history from one it WATCHED form. `barstate.ishistory` is true on bars that were already in the chart when the script started and false on bars the script saw arrive, so two viewers opening the same symbol at different times disagree about the same bar — and a viewer who leaves a chart open sees a bar change its answer without any data changing.
rows.why_it_matters: ⛔ A SCRIPT THAT BRANCHES ON THE TWO HAS ONE UNREACHABLE BRANCH HERE, AND THE MEMBER CANNOT SEE THAT FROM THE OUTPUT. `if barstate.ishistory … else …` runs the first arm on every bar we evaluate; the second arm is not refused, it simply never fires, which is the failure mode `lesson_an_over_refusal_is_invisible` is the mirror of. ⭐ AND THE DIRECTION IS THE SAFE ONE FOR A SCREEN: the arm that runs is the one the vendor runs on historical bars, which is every bar a scan ever reads. It is the PANE where a member could notice, and the pane's data notes say so.
rows.what_would_settle_it: A capture on a live TradingView chart reading `barstate.ishistory` and `barstate.isrealtime` on the newest bar during RTH and again after the close, plus a second reading from a chart opened AFTER those bars formed. The second reading is the one that proves the viewer-dependence rather than assuming it — which is why this row is `reasoned` and not `measured`.
rows.ours_is_deliberate: ⭐ THIS IS NOT A BUG TO FIX. A viewer-dependent answer is one this engine must not reproduce: two members running the same saved definition on the same symbol would get different columns, and a sweep would disagree with the pane that produced it. The vendor's behaviour makes sense for a chart somebody is watching and does not survive being SAVED.
rows.code: app/src/components/chart/indicators.js::computeClock (CLOCK_EXTENT and CLOCK_REALTIME); the Python twin is api/services/indicator_compute.py::compute_clock

probe.case: `plot(barstate.ishistory ? 1 : 0)` on a chart opened BEFORE a bar forms, read on that bar after it closes — and the same script on a chart opened AFTER it formed, read on the same bar
probe.under_ours: 1 on both readings. The bar's period has ended, and nothing in a static fetch records who was watching when.
probe.under_theirs: 0 on the first reading and 1 on the second. The chart that watched the bar form classifies it as realtime-then-confirmed, never as loaded history.
probe.discriminates: ⭐ THE TWO READINGS ARE OF THE SAME BAR, so no float comparison and no tolerance is involved — the conventions disagree about a BOOLEAN, and one of them disagrees with itself between two viewers. ⛔ A probe that read only one chart could not tell them apart at all: on a chart opened after the fact the vendor answers exactly what we answer.

decision.ruled: 2026-09-09 — KEEP OURS, and the divergence is deliberate. A viewer-dependent answer is one a SAVED definition must not carry: two members running the same script on the same symbol would get different columns, and a sweep would disagree with the pane that produced it.
decision.what_we_do_instead: `ishistory` means `isconfirmed` — the bar's period has ended — which is what the vendor's column reduces to for every bar a scan ever reads. The member is told through the manifest's `_barstate.vendorNote`, which reaches the paste box through the same walk `atr`'s note does.
decision.not_a_backlog_item: ⛔ THERE IS NOTHING TO FIX HERE. Reproducing the vendor would mean recording WHO WAS WATCHING in a saved definition, which is not a property of the market and cannot survive being stored.
decision.why_keep_ours: ⛔ A VIEWER-DEPENDENT ANSWER CANNOT SURVIVE BEING SAVED. The vendor’s `ishistory` records who was watching when the bar formed; a definition stored in our database is read by a pane, a sweep, an alert and a share link, and none of them was watching anything. Reproducing it would mean two members getting different columns from the same script on the same symbol — the property every consumer in `refused_by` depends on NOT happening. ⭐ AND THE ARM WE RUN IS THE ARM A SCAN WOULD ALWAYS TAKE: every bar a screener reads is historical to the vendor too, so for the contract where this matters most the two agree exactly.
decision.what_would_reopen_it: A capture showing the vendor’s `ishistory` is NOT viewer-dependent after all — i.e. two charts opened at different times agreeing about the same bar — would make this an ordinary difference we should simply match. ⚠️ So would a product decision to evaluate a LIVE, streaming series rather than a static fetch: the distinction would then have a referent here, and the column would have to be re-derived rather than aliased.
